title: Pointers, Addresses and Pointer Declarations
learningObjectives: Explain pointers, addresses and pointer declarations.
Describe pointer/reference or lifetime rules involved.
Trace a simple memory access or ownership operation.
Recognize common undefined behavior and safety risks.
Choose a safer approach for a practical task.

understand.concept: A pointer variable stores an address of an object. The pointer type indicates the type of object it points to; use & to obtain an object's address.
understand.whyItMatters: Pointers are fundamental to APIs, dynamic objects, iterators and indirect access.
understand.explain: Initialize pointers, understand what object they refer to, and avoid invalid addresses.

examples.title: Address and pointer
examples.explanation: ptr stores the address of score.

examples.title: Typed pointer
examples.explanation: The pointer type matches the object type.

examples.title: Pointer initialized to null
examples.code: int* p=nullptr;\n// p currently points to no int object
examples.explanation: nullptr clearly represents an empty pointer.

examples.title: Change pointer target
examples.explanation: The pointer can be reassigned to another object of compatible type.

examples.title: Address operator
examples.code: int value=7;\nint* p=&value;\n*p=9; // value is now 9

practise.guidedTask: Trace the five Pointers, Addresses and Pointer Declarations examples. Mark each pointer/reference's target, object lifetime, mutability and whether dereferencing is valid.
practise.independentTask: Build a small C++ exercise showing pointers, addresses and pointer declarations. Include safe cases and deliberately describe (but do not execute) one invalid case. Demonstrate how ownership or lifetime is managed.
hints: Draw pointer arrows to live objects.
Use nullptr for empty pointers and check before dereferencing.
Keep pointer arithmetic within one array.
Distinguish pointer constness from pointee constness.
Prefer value returns, containers and smart pointers to manual ownership.
